vocab.definition: pH below 7 — source of H⁺ ions.
a soluble base, pH above 7 — source of OH⁻ ions.

misconceptions.wrong: A high pH means a strong acid.
misconceptions.right: High pH means alkaline; low pH means acidic.
Only bases that dissolve in water are alkalis.
Neutral (pH 7) has equal H⁺ and OH⁻.

questions.text: State the pH range of an acid and an alkali. [2 marks]
Name the ion responsible for acidity and the ion for alkalinity. [2 marks]
Write the ionic equation for neutralisation. [2 marks]
Name two ways to measure the pH of a solution. [2 marks]
Complete the sentence using the word bank. [2 marks]
questions.secondaryText: In neutralisation, ______ ions react with ______ ions to make water.

questions.text: Suggest why farmers add lime to acidic soil. [1 mark]

footer.tip: Acids release H⁺; alkalis release OH⁻; they combine to make neutral water.
footer.thinkPrompt: Why does each step down the pH scale mean 10× more H⁺ ions?
